items.label: f08-audit-trail-events
items.front: How w22 keeps an audit trail of each payment, and the risk if it were wrong
items.back: PaymentEvent rows are appended through one write boundary, createPaymentEvent() in paymentEventRepository, which the payment, refund, webhook and reconciliation services all call; PaymentDetailsCard renders the trail for operators. If wrong, operators lose the historical sequence needed to explain incidents or financial anomalies.

items.label: f01-three-fixes
items.front: Three standard fixes for concurrent over-refunds under READ COMMITTED
items.back: 1) Lock the payment row first (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE) so B waits for A. 2) Run at Serializable isolation and retry on serialization failure. 3) Keep a running refundedMinor on Payment and update it with a guarded atomic UPDATE ... WHERE refunded + n <= amount, treating zero rows as 409.

items.label: f04-webhook-dup-check-outside-tx
items.front: What happens when one provider event is delivered twice concurrently?
items.back: The duplicate check reads the event before the transaction, so both deliveries proceed; the second createWebhookEvent hits the providerEventId unique constraint and surfaces as a 500.

items.label: f03-errors-as-contract
items.front: How jsonError maps errors, and why the refund service catches nothing
items.back: RouteError -> { error: { code, message, details } } with its status; ZodError -> 400; anything else -> logged 500. The service lets non-domain errors propagate so infrastructure failures stay distinguishable from domain refusals.

items.label: f11-staff-role-permissions
items.front: w22's staff roles: what SUPPORT, OPS and ADMIN may do, and where the map lives
items.back: src/lib/permissions.ts holds the explicit role-to-permission map. SUPPORT can read any payment but cannot create, refund, deliver webhooks or run reconciliation. OPS can create payments, read any payment, refund, deliver webhooks and run reconciliation. ADMIN has the same operational permissions as OPS.

items.label: f05-multitenancy-retrofit
items.front: w22 is not multi-tenant. The auth doc's five steps to add tenancy later without a rewrite
items.back: 1) Add tenantId to tenant-owned models (Payment, ProviderPayment, WebhookDelivery, WebhookEvent, Refund, ReconciliationIssue). 2) Extend AuthenticatedSession with tenantId. 3) Make buildPaymentListScope() return tenant and ownership filters. 4) Make every repository read of tenant-owned data scope by tenantId before business filters. 5) Add a tenant-aware permission layer beside permissions.ts so platform admins and org operators are separated.

items.label: f10-zod-validation-boundary
items.front: Where w22 draws its Zod validation boundary, and what goes wrong without it
items.back: createPaymentSchema and refundPaymentSchema live in src/lib/validation/paymentSchemas.ts; the payments route and the refund route call .parse() before any business logic. Without that boundary, malformed money values or weak refund reasons reach service code and fail later in less predictable ways.

items.label: f09-shipped-test-risks
items.front: The four shipped .test.ts files: the risk each guards, and which one needs installed dependencies
items.back: SUPPORT cannot run reconciliation: a privileged action exposing system-wide financial state, so RBAC must be trustworthy. FAILED cannot move back to SUCCEEDED: terminal-state regressions create false revenue or refund eligibility. CUSTOMER list scope: list endpoints are the easiest place to leak multi-record data. Non-positive amounts rejected: amount validation belongs at the API boundary. Only the schema test imports zod; the other three import local source and node: modules.

items.label: f02-simulated-provider
items.front: Why moving reads into the transaction does not solve real provider coordination
items.back: The provider refund id is generated locally (prov_ref_<uuid>) with no external call. A real provider refund can succeed after the DB transaction rolls back, or vice versa; that needs an outbox or a request-then-confirm-via-webhook design.

items.label: f06-layer-map-reading-order
items.front: w22's folder layers, and the reading order the architecture overview recommends
items.back: src/app: pages and HTTP entrypoints. src/components: client UI that calls React Query hooks. src/hooks: the browser data boundary that calls REST and owns cache invalidation. src/services: business logic. src/repositories: the database boundary. src/lib: cross-cutting policy and domain rules. prisma/schema.prisma: relational source of truth. Read schema, permissions.ts, paymentService, webhookService, reconciliationService: schema first, policy second, write path third, async correction paths fourth.

items.label: f07-entity-owning-services
items.front: Which service is the primary owner of each w22 entity?
items.back: authService: User and Session. paymentService: IdempotencyRecord and Payment. providerSimulatorService: PaymentAttempt, ProviderPayment and WebhookDelivery. webhookService: WebhookEvent. refundService: Refund. reconciliationService: ReconciliationRun and ReconciliationIssue.
